transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’m here because I haven’t been handling things too well since my daughter left for basic training. I mean, I know kids grow up and I should be proud, and I am, but… the house feels dead when I come home now.

I’ve been trying to keep it together, but I’m crying in my truck before shifts sometimes, and at work I’m missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years. I’ve snapped at some of the younger guys too, which isn’t really me. And I’ve pretty much stopped doing the things I usually like, like going out on the water or working on my sculpture. I just… don’t see the point right now. I’m sorry, I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you need to hear.
How long have you been feeling this way since your daughter left for basic training?
About a month, I guess. Since she left for basic training, that’s when it really started. I kept thinking it would settle down after a few days, but… yeah, it’s been pretty much since then.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

Not really… I mean, I’m trying not to make it sound worse than it is, but the things I usually like just aren’t doing much for me right now. I used to go out on the water, or work on my sculpture, and that would kind of settle me. Since my daughter left, I just come home and the house feels so empty, and I can’t get myself to care about doing any of it.

I don’t know if that answers it right, but… no, I’m not really finding much pleasure in things lately.
Have you had any thoughts of not wanting to live or wishing you were dead?

I… I don’t think so. Not like that. I mean, I’ve felt really low and overwhelmed, but I’m not sitting there wishing I was dead or anything. I don’t want you to think I’m… you know, unsafe. It’s more like I just don’t know what to do with myself right now.
Have you noticed any change in your weight since your daughter left for basic training?

Um… I’m not really sure. I haven’t been weighing myself or anything. My clothes don’t feel hugely different, I don’t think. Maybe a little off, but I couldn’t tell you if I’ve actually lost or gained weight. Is that okay?
Have you been feeling unusually anxious or on edge since your daughter left for basic training?

Yeah… I guess I have been. I keep trying to tell myself it’s just me adjusting and that I should be handling it better, but since she left I come home and the house just feels… dead. And then I feel like I can’t keep myself together.

I’ve been crying in my truck before work sometimes, before my shifts, which is embarrassing. And at work I’m missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years, or I’ll snap at the younger guys over stupid stuff. I don’t mean to. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything. I’m just… on edge a lot more than I want to admit.
Are there any days where you feel a little better and want to do something you used to enjoy?

I wish I could say yes. I mean… there are moments where I think maybe I should go out on the water or work on my sculpture again, because those used to help me. But then I get home and the house just feels so empty, and I kind of lose the point of it.

I don’t want to sound dramatic. It’s just since my daughter left, I haven’t really been doing those things. Mostly I’m just trying to get through work without messing up or getting short with people. Does that make sense?
Do you feel sad or depressed most of the day?

Most of the day… yeah, I think so. I keep wanting to say it’s not that bad, because I’m still going to work and doing what I’m supposed to do, mostly. But since my daughter left, it’s like I come home and the house just feels dead, and then I kind of fall apart.

I’ve been crying in my truck before shifts sometimes, and I’m not really doing the things I used to enjoy, like going out on the water or working on my sculpture. I just… don’t see the point lately. I’m sorry, that sounds awful. But yeah, I guess I do feel sad a lot of the day.
Are there any activities that you've completely stopped doing since your daughter left?

Yeah… I’ve pretty much stopped going out on the water. I used to do that to clear my head, and I haven’t really been doing it at all since she left.

And my sculpture stuff too. I keep telling myself I’ll get back to it, but then I come home and the house feels so empty, and I just… don’t see the point. I know that probably sounds like I’m letting it get to me too much, but that’s what’s been happening.
Do you feel guilty about anything in particular since your daughter left for basic training?

I don’t know… not guilty about one specific thing, I guess. I mean, I keep wondering if I should’ve handled it better or been more supportive, but I don’t have some big thing I did wrong that I can point to.

I’m probably overthinking it. I just don’t want to make it seem like I’m blaming her or anything.
Are there any things that you used to enjoy that you still find pleasure in, even if it's just a little bit?

A little, maybe… but not much. I’m trying to think of something that still feels good and I don’t want to sound dramatic, but most of the things I used to look forward to just feel kind of pointless right now.

Like going out on the water used to help me settle down, and my sculpture was something I could lose myself in. Since my daughter left, I just come home and the house feels so dead, and I can’t really make myself do either one. I keep telling myself I’ll get back to them, but… I haven’t.
Are there any activities that you've found yourself having no interest in at all since your daughter left?

Yeah… I guess the big ones are the water and my sculpture. I used to really want that time, you know? Being out on the water would settle me, and working on a piece would kind of pull me out of my head.

Since she left for basic, I just… I come home and the house feels dead, and I can’t make myself care about doing any of it. I know that sounds bad, I’m not trying to be dramatic. It’s just like I don’t see the point right now.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?

Honestly… not really. I mean, I’m sure there are little moments here and there, but the things that used to actually feel good—going out on the water, working on my sculpture—I’ve pretty much stopped doing them.

Since my daughter left for basic, I come home and the house just feels… dead. And I know that probably sounds like too much, but I just don’t see the point right now.
Have you noticed a significant decrease in interest in activities you usually enjoy since your daughter left?

Yeah… yes, I have. I’m trying not to make it sound bigger than it is, but since she left for basic, I just come home and the house feels dead.

I used to go out on the water, or work on my sculpture, and now I just… don’t. I keep thinking I should make myself do it, but I can’t seem to care enough. It feels like there’s no point, if that makes sense.
How long have you noticed a decrease in interest in the things you usually enjoy?
I think… about a month now. Since my daughter left, really. I keep hoping it’s just me adjusting and I’ll snap out of it, but yeah, I’ve been struggling with not caring about those things since then.
Would you say that you have lost interest in almost all activities you usually enjoyed?

I guess… yeah, pretty much. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but the things I used to really look forward to, like going out on the water or working on my sculpture, I’ve just stopped. Since my daughter left for basic, I come home and the house feels so empty, and I just don’t see the point in doing any of it right now.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight since your daughter left for basic training?
Um… I don’t think so. I haven’t really been keeping track closely, but I haven’t noticed my clothes fitting a lot differently or anything like that. So I’d say no, not a significant amount.
Would you say that there's been a big drop in how much you enjoy the things you're still doing, even if you're not doing as many of them?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I still get through some things because I have to, but it feels like there’s no real enjoyment in it. Since my daughter left for basic, I come home and it’s like the house is just… dead, and I don’t really look forward to anything.

Even stuff I used to love, like going out on the water or working on my sculpture, I just don’t see the point right now. I know that probably sounds kind of bad… but that’s honestly how it feels.
Would you say that you have lost almost all interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. I’m sorry, I know I already kind of said that, but yes. Since my daughter left for basic training, it’s like I come home to this dead house and I just… I can’t get myself to care about the things I used to.

I’ve stopped going out on the water, and I haven’t been working on my sculpture. Those were things I really loved, and now I just don’t see the point. I don’t mean that to sound dramatic, but that’s the honest answer.
Have your symptoms lasted for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yeah… I think it has. It’s been about a month since my daughter left, and I’ve been kind of struggling like this since then. I mean, I’m still getting through the day, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but… most days, most of the day, yes.
